title: Task-based model routing
summary: Choose the least expensive route that satisfies the task’s measured acceptance criteria.

sections.label: Proposed routing policy
items: Use deterministic code for structured parsing, calculations, dates, permissions, schema checks, and execution.
Use a utility model for bounded tasks with readily checkable outputs.
Use a main implementation model for normal repository analysis and changes.
Route difficult or consequential interpretation directly to a stronger model when justified.
Escalate on a defined condition: contradictory evidence, unresolved diagnosis, or failed verification.

sections.label: Avoid repeated work
sections.text: Do not pass every task through every model tier. A second model needs a specific purpose, such as a different investigation or independently checking a difficult finding.

sections.label: Acceptance
sections.text: Routing is backed by held-out task results, cost, latency, and review effort rather than model reputation alone.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
sections.text: Compare feasible routes for the task, plan held out evaluation cases and choose the route from observed acceptance, resource use and escalation behavior. The workflow placement and checks are Atlas recommendations. Only the source contribution below was verified on 15 October 2026, not every original assertion or project outcome.

sections.label: Gap review: acceptance outputs
items: A routing policy records the task classes, acceptance thresholds, deterministic path and explicit escalation conditions.
A held out result table compares candidates on the same inputs and reports failures, cost, latency and review effort.
A recommendation states supported task scope and unresolved limits, with an escalation example checked or explicitly unrun.

sections.label: Gap review: verified source contribution
sections.text: Anthropic distinguishes task success criteria, repeated trials, grading logic and final outcomes, and describes tracking cost and latency on evaluation tasks. The source supports evaluation design and metrics. It does not prove the proposed routing tiers, a cheapest acceptable model or superiority for the project workload. Review date: 15 October 2026. This review covers this source contribution only, not the whole guide.

catalog.applicability: Use when deciding which work goes to deterministic code, a utility model, the main implementation model or a stronger model, and on which condition to escalate. Back the routing with held out task results, cost, latency and review effort rather than model reputation.
catalog.limits: Reading a topic does not configure tools, execute a workflow or establish passing evidence.
